The Woman

precepts.text: The Lord has likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman. That is the woman Revelation 12 is talking about: the twelve tribes of Israel.
precepts.point: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God. The wilderness is Africa; we fled out of Jerusalem into Africa, the same place where Joseph took the young child and his mother. Then a place was prepared, which is the Americas. A thousand two hundred and threescore days: 1260 days, three and a half, the same period written as forty and two months and as a time, times, and the dividing of time in Daniel 7 and 8.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
“And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun.” Who is this woman? Jeremiah says, “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” The Lord has likened his people to a comely, delicate woman.

So that is the woman Revelation 12 is talking about: the twelve tribes of Israel. Keep that in mind through the whole chapter. “upon her head a crown of twelve stars”: the twelve stars are the twelve tribes, which is why she is called that way.

When “she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered”, it is the nation of Israel travailing to bring forth Christ, to save us from the hand of the Romans who had taken the kingdom of Israel by force. Pained to be delivered means we were persecuted. Everything that happens to the woman in this chapter is the history of our people.

precepts.text: Ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein; the old religions will have to go means the law and the commandments have to go, and they said we will not walk therein.
precepts.point: The 1960s and the 1990s were the two waves: the truth began in 1969 and the one-West teachers came in the 1990s, so Esau hit each wave with the Bible revisions, the vaccine schedule, crack, the three-strikes law and the prison pipeline.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
Daniel says the beast shall “think to change times and laws”, and the plan laid out at the 1969 meeting of the order, delivered by Dr. Richard Day, spoke of changing laws and customs in so many words. One of its points was blending all religions: the old religions will have to go. Old means us, teaching the old ways. That is Jeremiah's old paths.

“Thus saith the Lord, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.” The old path is the good way, the laws and commandments of God, and you find rest for your souls in it. Getting rid of the old religions means getting rid of us and bringing all nations together as one, Babylon together again, with all the old teachings of the laws and commandments of God taken out.

“But they said, We will not walk therein.” Our people say, no, we don't want to; Christianity is better, I can do what I want.

That is why the new religion they planned would take something from all the old ones so people could feel at home in it. Christianity is a doctrine of adaptation: do what the world does, go to the club, do what you want, as long as you believe in white Jesus. Islam is a doctrine of adaptation: no pork, but eat everything else, and women wear pants. In the truth you can't eat what you want, wear what you want and do what you want. That is the old way, and that is what they say has to go. Even Israelites are starting to adapt, going to the clubs and wearing snap-on fringes they can take off and put back on.

So changing times and laws is not only the calendar. It is turning our people from the old paths, where the rest for our souls is found.

precepts.text: I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman. That is how the Lord sees his people.
precepts.point: I will surely avenge them; my people is led as a flock to the slaughter; I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt, but bring them out with a mighty hand and smite Egypt with plagues as before and destroy all the land thereof. As before means a coming Egypt, the United States. When it comes, we do not want to go down with it.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The first author of beauty is our God, and he looked at us as beautiful. That is why he refers to us as a woman: “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.”

Comely means beautiful, handsome. That is how the Lord looks at his people: the daughter of Zion is a comely and delicate woman in his eyes.

That is why he says in 2 Esdras that “the innocent and righteous blood crieth unto me”, that “my people is led as a flock to the slaughter”, and that he will surely avenge them. All the murders and injustice done to God's children here in spiritual Egypt are done to the daughter he likened to a comely and delicate woman, and he will not suffer them to dwell in that Egypt any more.

precepts.text: From the least to the greatest every one is given to covetousness, and from the prophet to the priest every one dealeth falsely.
precepts.point: The prophets of Samaria, the northern Latino tribes, prophesied in Baal; the prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery and walk in lies, from December 25 to the ever-virgin Mary, and strengthen the hands of evildoers so the white man can do no wrong. They are all to God as Sodom and Gomorrah.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “Mine heart within me is broken because of the prophets”: the pastors who destroy and scatter the sheep. “For both prophet and priest are profane; yea, in my house have I found their wickedness”. In the prophets of Jerusalem he saw “an horrible thing: they commit adultery, and walk in lies”. The whole church system of Christianity is lies: Jesus born December 25th, Jesus a white man, Mary never having relations with Joseph, the ever virgin who never had children. All lies. “they strengthen also the hands of evildoers”: the white man can do no wrong.

Jeremiah 6:13 shows the root of it: “For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely.”

Everyone is given to covetousness, so we all have to be mindful of that covetous spirit, especially among the prophets, the pastors and the shepherds. All these pastors deal falsely, and God says “they are all of them unto me as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrah.”

precepts.text: The daughter of Zion is likened to a comely and delicate woman; the woman of the vision is Israel.
precepts.point: The dream came true. In the famine the whole house of Jacob came down to Joseph in Egypt, and he placed them in the best of the land and nourished them with bread; they bowed to the one the Most High had set over them.

note.label: Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer

precepts.why:
“I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” The daughter of Zion is the nation of Israel, and she is likened to a woman.

That is who the woman clothed with the sun with the crown of twelve stars is: Israel, and the twelve stars her tribes. Joseph's dream of the sun, the moon and the eleven stars bowing to him is the same picture of the house of Jacob, which Jacob read at once as himself, Joseph's mother and his brethren.

precepts.text: I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words nor to my law; evil is another way of saying curses.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
What are curses? “Hear, O earth: behold, I will bring evil upon this people, even the fruit of their thoughts, because they have not hearkened unto my words, nor to my law, but rejected it.” Evil is another way of saying curses. And the reason is the same reason Deuteronomy gives: they have not hearkened unto his words nor to his law; they rejected it.

So “all these curses shall come upon thee” is the Most High bringing evil upon Israel for not hearkening to his voice, which is his commandments, and that evil is the fruit of their own thoughts.

precepts.text: Stand in the ways and ask for the old paths and walk therein; but they said we will not.
precepts.point: Remember His marvelous works, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth. The Bible tells us to remember our past.

note.label: Psalm 105: Remember His Marvelous Works from Abraham to the Exodus

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.” Remembering his marvellous works and the judgments of his mouth is asking for the old paths, the good way our fathers walked, and the rest for our souls is found in walking in it.

“But they said, We will not walk therein.” Israel refused. The psalm calls us the other way: give thanks unto the Lord, call upon his name, glory in his holy name and remember what he has done, so that we do not answer as they did.

precepts.text: Stand and ask for the old paths, the good way, and walk in it to find rest for your souls; but they said they would not walk therein.
precepts.point: David remembers the days of old and meditates on the works and the hands of the Most High. The days of old matter for us today, because our oppressor wants us to forget our past while he never forgets his own. They always remember 9/11 and the so-called holocaust; they do not forget their history, but they want us to forget ours.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.” David remembers the days of old and meditates on the works of the Most High; we are told to ask for the old paths, the good way, and walk in it to find rest for our souls.

Our oppressor wants us to forget our past while he never forgets his own. They always remember 9/11 and the so-called holocaust; they do not forget their history, but they want us to forget ours, and like those who said “We will not walk therein”, many will not go back to the old paths.

precepts.text: They are greedy dogs that can never have enough and shepherds that cannot understand, every one looking to his own way and his own gain.
precepts.point: From the least to the greatest every one is given to covetousness, and from the prophet to the priest every one deals falsely, for the priests were only about gain at this time.

note.label: Jeremiah 6: The Ancient Nation from the North

precepts.why:
“Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter.” That is the prophet and the priest of Jeremiah's day: “from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely.” The priests were only about gain at this time, greedy dogs that can never have enough, every one looking to his own way and his own gain.

And it ran through the whole people: “from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness”. Shepherds that cannot understand cannot lead a people out of covetousness when they are given to it themselves.

precepts.text: The Most High stopped accepting the multitude of sacrifices, having no delight in the blood of bullocks, lambs, and goats from a sinful people that kept on sinning.
precepts.point: Incense from Sheba and sweet cane from a far country are of no purpose; their burnt offerings and sacrifices are not acceptable to Him.

note.label: Jeremiah 6: The Ancient Nation from the North

precepts.why:
“To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the Lord: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.” The Most High stopped accepting the multitude of sacrifices, having no delight in the blood of bullocks, lambs, and goats from a sinful people that kept on sinning.

Jeremiah says the same: “To what purpose cometh there to me incense from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country? your burnt offerings are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices sweet unto me.” The offerings are of no purpose because “they have not hearkened unto my words, nor to my law, but rejected it.” So he brings evil upon this people, even the fruit of their thoughts, and no incense or sacrifice turns it away.

precepts.text: The Most High likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman, and that comely delicate woman is Israel.
precepts.point: He appeared of old saying He loved them with an everlasting love and with lovingkindness drew them; again He will build the virgin of Israel, adorned with her tabrets and going forth in the dances, planting vines on the mountains of Samaria until the watchmen on Mount Ephraim cry, Arise, let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God.

note.label: Jeremiah 31: The New Covenant

precepts.why:
The Lord says “Again I will build thee, and thou shalt be built, O virgin of Israel”, adorned with her tabrets and going forth in the dances of them that make merry. Earlier in Jeremiah he tells who that virgin is: “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.”

That comely and delicate woman is Israel. The daughter of Zion, the virgin of Israel, is the people he loved with an everlasting love and drew with lovingkindness, the same people left of the sword that found grace in the wilderness. He will build her again, and she will plant vines on the mountains of Samaria until the watchmen on Mount Ephraim cry, Arise, let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God.

precepts.text: Stand in the ways and ask for the old paths, the good way, and walk therein to find rest for your souls, though they said we will not; the old paths are keeping God's laws.
precepts.point: Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel.

note.label: Jeremiah 31: The New Covenant

precepts.why:
The Lord will lead the gathered remnant “in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble”. That straight way is keeping God's laws. He had told our fathers where to find it: “Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.”

The old paths are keeping God's laws; that is the good way and the rest for our souls. “But they said, We will not walk therein.” Our fathers refused the old paths, and that is why Israel had to be brought back from the north country with weeping and supplications. When he gathers them he leads them in that same straight way himself.

precepts.text: The Most High keeps referring to Israel as her because he has likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman, a bride.
precepts.point: He will sow her unto himself in the earth, have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy, and say to them which were not his people, Thou art my people, and they shall say, Thou art my God. This is what is going on now as all people are repenting.

note.label: Hosea 2: Plead With Your Mother

precepts.why:
“I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy”. The Most High keeps referring to Israel as her. “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” Israel is his bride, a comely and delicate woman, and that is why she is her.

He will say “to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.” This is what is going on now as all people are repenting.
